newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Telecoms Council calls for self-regulation of Internet.
newsitem.headline: Telecoms Council calls for self-regulation of Internet.

text.p: European Union countries should promote self-regulation and ratings systems to control illegal and harmful material on the Internet, the Telecommunications Council said on Thursday.

The ministers echoed the approach proposed last month by the European Commission, which shied away from advocating strict new legislation to protect children or prevent criminals from misusing the global computer network.
They said in a resolution that EU governments should promote solutions such as industry codes of conduct, self-regulatory bodies and hotlines for the public.

They should also encourage the use of technologies such as the Platform for Internet Content Selection (PICS), which allows Internet users to filter out sexually explicit or other unwanted material through the use of ratings systems, the ministers said.
The ministers also asked the Commission to examine the question of legal liability.

The Commission, which issued a communication and green paper on the Internet last month, said governments should consider whether an EU legal framework was needed to clarify whether Internet acess or service providers were liable for illegal content such as child pornography, copyright infringements, libel or fraudulent material.

The Council also said EU governments should promote international cooperation on the question of harmful and illegal Internet content and participate actively in a global ministerial conference on the issue that Germany plans to host.
